subject: Polity
description: Covers Zero hour, Starred questions, Adjournment motion, Quorum.

questions.stem: In the context of the Indian Parliament, what does the term 'Zero Hour' refer to?

options.option_text: The time immediately following the Question Hour when members can raise matters of urgent public importance without prior notice
The first hour of every parliamentary sitting dedicated exclusively to the Prime Minister's speech
The period when Parliament is prorogued by the President
A strictly regulated hour where voting on Constitutional Amendment Bills takes place

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: 'Zero Hour' is an Indian parliamentary innovation (not mentioned in the official rules of procedure). It starts immediately after the Question Hour (around 12:00 noon, hence the name 'Zero Hour'). During this time, Members of Parliament (MPs) can raise matters of urgent public importance without giving the mandatory 10 days' prior notice required during Question Hour.
DECOY BUSTING: The FIRST hour of every parliamentary sitting (11:00 AM to 12:00 noon) is the 'Question Hour', where MPs ask questions to ministers and hold the government accountable. Prorogation is the end of a session. Voting has no specific 'hour'.
EXAM INSIGHT: Because there is no prior notice, ministers are not bound to reply to issues raised during Zero Hour, making it a time of great chaos and political grandstanding.

questions.stem: During the 'Question Hour' in Parliament, what is a 'Starred Question'?

options.option_text: A question that requires an oral answer on the floor of the House, allowing members to ask supplementary questions
A question that requires a written reply, after which no supplementary questions can be asked
A question asked by a private member to another private member, rather than to a minister
A question related exclusively to matters of national security and defense

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: A Starred Question (distinguished by an asterisk mark *) is one for which an ORAL answer is desired by the member on the floor of the House. Because the minister gives the answer orally, other members can immediately ask 'supplementary questions' to cross-examine the minister on the spot.
DECOY BUSTING: 
- An 'Unstarred Question' requires a written reply. Since it's written and placed on the table, no supplementary questions can be asked. 
- A 'Short Notice Question' is asked orally on matters of urgent public importance with less than 10 days' notice.
EXAM INSIGHT: Starred questions are printed in Green ink, Unstarred in White ink, and Short Notice questions in Light Pink ink in the parliamentary lists.

questions.stem: Which motion is introduced in the Lok Sabha to draw the attention of the House to a definite matter of urgent public importance, and requires the support of 50 members to be admitted?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Adjournment Motion is an extraordinary procedure. If admitted, it sets aside the normal business of the House to discuss a definite matter of urgent public importance (like a massive train derailment or a terrorist attack). It requires the support of 50 members to be admitted. It is considered a censure against the government, hence it is only permitted in the Lok Sabha, not in the Rajya Sabha.
DECOY BUSTING: A No-Confidence Motion is to prove the government lacks a majority. A Calling Attention Motion asks a minister to make a statement on an urgent matter, but it does not censure the government or interrupt normal business as drastically. A Privilege Motion is moved when a minister commits a breach of parliamentary privilege.
EXAM INSIGHT: The discussion on an Adjournment Motion must last for not less than two hours and thirty minutes.

questions.stem: What is the quorum required to constitute a meeting of either House of Parliament?

options.option_text: One-tenth of the total number of members of the House
One-third of the total number of members of the House
One-half of the total number of members of the House
Two-thirds of the members present and voting

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Quorum is the minimum number of members required to be present in the House before it can transact any business. According to Article 100 of the Constitution, the quorum for either House of Parliament is one-tenth (1/10th) of the total number of members of the House (including the presiding officer). 
DECOY BUSTING: This means there must be at least 55 members present in the Lok Sabha (out of 543) and 25 members present in the Rajya Sabha (out of 245). If there is no quorum, it is the duty of the Speaker/Chairman to either adjourn the House or suspend the meeting until there is a quorum.
EXAM INSIGHT: Two-thirds of members present and voting is the special majority required for passing constitutional amendment bills or impeaching the President, not for a daily quorum.
